job.style: a passage that starts from a common wrong idea and corrects it

response.passage: Many students mistakenly believe that Johannes Gutenberg invented the concept of movable type, but he actually refined existing technologies from East Asia. While woodblock printing was common in China, Gutenberg developed the mechanical printing press in Europe during the 1430s. This innovation did not instantly transform society, nor did it immediately grant literacy to every woman in India. In fact, the growth of female literacy in India was a gradual process supported by reformers and schools, rather than an overnight miracle caused by the arrival of the press. Furthermore, colonial authorities were deeply concerned about the influence of local publications. The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was introduced to control the content of newspapers published in Indian languages, but it did not shut down every single publication in the country. Instead, it empowered the government to censor critical reports and seize printing machinery from those who published seditious material. By understanding these nuances, we see that print culture was a complex tool that evolved through political struggle and social reform, rather than a sudden, uniform force that changed everything instantly without resistance or limitation.
response.summary: Print technology evolved from earlier Asian methods rather than appearing suddenly with Gutenberg. Its impact on literacy and political control in India was a gradual process rather than an immediate, total transformation.
